newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North see substantial Alumbrera profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North see substantial Alumbrera profit.

text.p: Australian mining and forestry group North Ltd expected substantial profits from its 25 percent interest in the Alumbrera gold and copper project in Argentina even at current copper prices, managing director Campbell Anderson said on Thursday.
Anderson said the Alumbrera project, which is due to begin production from August 1997, had assumed a long term copper price not far from current prices.
Alumbrera, which is expected to produce 180,000 tonnes of copper and 640,000 ounces of gold a year, was a very low cost producer, he said.
"I don't think one should look too pessimistically at the current copper prices. They've not bombed out entirely," Anderson told reporters after the group's annual meeting.

"When we went into Alumbrera, we did not assume a long run copper price significantly higher than the present one," he said. "It's a very low cost mine because it's got substantial gold credits, but in any event, the costs of the copper and gold are very very low," he added.
Anderson agreed Alumbrera would produce substantial profit growth at current copper prices.
Earlier, Chairman Michael Deeley said projects like Alumbrera would lift profits substantially from 1998/99 and beyond.
But Deeley said the outlook was for flat trading in the current year to June 30, 1996.
MIM Holdings Ltd chief executive Nick Stump said last week that massive gold credits meant the net copper cost of the Alumbrera project was below 30 U.S. cents.
MIM is 50 percent owner and operator of Alumbrera. North Ltd and Rio Algom Ltd own 25 percent.

Alumbrera, in Argentina's northwestern province of Catamarca, is scheduled to start production by August 1997, working up to an annual rate of 700,000 tonnes of intermediate mine concentrate containing 180,000 tonnes of copper metal.
Anderson also said North would hedge forward its copper sales from Alumbrera once production began, as it had done for its Northparkes copper/gold mine in New South Wales.
"We will be undoubtedly putting in some copper hedging in future in a similar style to what we have for Northparkes," he said, adding he saw a similar percentage of hedging.
Currently, North's copper sales from Northparkes are 76 percent hedged for 1996/97, 46 percent hedged for 1997/98 and 26 percent hedged for 1998/99.
North's shares were up six cents at A$3.60 at 1.30 p.m. (0230 GMT).
